question.problem: A triangle $△ABC$ has $m∠A={37}^{∘},$ $m∠B={90}^{∘},$ and $AC=25.$ Find $AB$ rounded to the nearest integer.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

First, let's sketch the given triangle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203245/assets/70ac3cbbc7209f71bd8095bb725d1dbb847c827bdfdc8220c25115fb120532b4.png)

First, note that we are given the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AC}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{AB}$ adjacent to the given angle $∠A.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is *cosine*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({37}^{∘}) & =\frac{AB}{25} \\ AB & =25\operatorname{cos}⁡({37}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =25\operatorname{cos}⁡({37}^{∘}) \\  & =25(0.798\,63…) \\  & =19.965\,88… \\  & ≈20,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.
